articles.title: The tech that could make Marvell the next trillion dollar company
articles.body:
The sun is slowly but surely setting on copper interconnects, according to Marvell CEO Matt Murphy, who spoke at Computex this week. Within the next decade, the company expects photons to replace electrons and fundamentally transform how datacenters operate.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang predicted this shift could elevate Marvell to trillion-dollar status. With a current market cap of $191 billion, Marvell's stock surged 30 percent following the announcement.

The transition stems from physical limitations. As Murphy explained, "The distance a signal can travel over a copper cable is inversely proportional to the bandwidth, so every time you double the bandwidth, you have to cut the distance in half." Current 200 Gbps interconnects operate at roughly 2.5 meters, with Nvidia's next-generation hardware pushing speeds to 400 Gbps—halving range again.

Optical solutions offer greater distance capabilities but introduce challenges. Pluggable optics consume significant power and experience higher failure rates. Huang noted that optical systems would have added 20 kilowatts to Nvidia's already-demanding 120-kilowatt NVL72 rack system.

Marvell has positioned itself for this transition through strategic acquisitions: Inphi in 2020 for optoelectrical interconnects, Celestial AI for silicon photonics technology, and a $2 billion Nvidia investment announced in March.

The implications extend beyond performance metrics. Murphy envisions disaggregated architectures where CPUs, GPUs, memory, and storage operate independently, reconfigurable for optimal workload ratios. This represents a paradigm shift from current integrated server designs constrained by distance limitations.

However, competition looms. Broadcom, with a $2 trillion market cap and major hyperscaler customers including Google and Meta, has also accumulated silicon photonics and optics portfolios. CEO Hock Tan expects photonics adoption eventually, "but we are not quite there yet."

articles.title: Marvell Keynote at COMPUTEX 2026: The Future of AI Scaling Depends on Connectivity
articles.body: Marvell Technology, Inc. announced at its COMPUTEX 2026 keynote that the future of AI scaling fundamentally depends on connectivity. CEO Matt Murphy outlined the company's vision for optical interconnects replacing copper in AI data centers over the next decade. Key announcements included the Teralynx T100, the industry's first 102.4 Tbps switch silicon purpose-built for AI and cloud data center infrastructure. The T100 was architected from the ground up for AI, enabling the industry's lowest power consumption and lowest latency at this bandwidth tier. The switch operates under 1,000W, supports 512-port scale-out radix, and uses advanced 3nm process technology with a monolithic design. Multiple deployment options include ball grid array, co-packaged copper, and co-packaged optics. Sampling began in Q2 2026. Murphy presented a vision of a 'data center without distance' enabled by co-packaged optics (CPO), where CPUs, GPUs, memory, and storage can be dynamically disaggregated across facilities. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang made a surprise appearance during the keynote and declared Marvell 'the next trillion-dollar company.' Marvell characterized itself as 'the Switzerland of the industry' due to serving multiple AI silicon providers rather than competing directly with compute makers. The Teralynx T100 supports both scale-out deployments for large training clusters and scale-up deployments with emerging standards like Ethernet Scale-Up Networking (ESUN) and Ultra Ethernet Consortium (UEC) requirements.

articles.title: 젠슨 황 '1조달러 기업' 전망에 마벨 주가 33% 폭등
articles.body: 컴퓨텍스 2026 타이베이 행사(6월 2일)에서 엔비디아 CEO 젠슨 황이 마벨 테크놀로지의 미래 가치에 대해 강력한 발언을 했다. 황 CEO는 "AI의 유용한 시대가 도래했으므로 마벨의 기업 가치가 급등할 것"이라고 전망했다. 이 발언 이후 마벨 주가가 단일 거래일에 33% 급등하며 290.79달러를 기록했다. 이는 2000년 6월 이후 26년 만의 최대 일일 상승폭이다. 마벨 시가총액은 약 2,545억 달러에 달했다. 2026년 연초 대비 마벨 주가는 3배 상승했다. SK하이닉스는 메모리 생산용량을 5년 내 두 배로 늘리겠다고 공언했으며, ST마이크로일렉트로닉스는 2026년 데이터센터 매출 전망을 거의 두 배로 상향 조정했다. 엔비디아는 3개월 전 마벨에 20억 달러 지분 투자를 단행한 바 있다. 마벨은 AI 컴퓨팅 기업들에게 중립적인 위치에서 네트워킹 반도체를 공급하는 전략을 취하고 있으며, 젠슨 황의 공개적 지지는 데이터센터 광인터커넥트 전환의 핵심 수혜주로 마벨을 부각시켰다.

articles.title: AI Memory Shortage Locked Through 2030: Computex 2026 Brings Agent Economy, HBM Crisis
articles.body:
The chips powering artificial intelligence will remain critically scarce until at least 2030, according to announcements at Computex 2026 in Taipei. SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won warned that the global supply gap for high-bandwidth memory persists through the decade's end, announcing plans to double total wafer production capacity within five years. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang subsequently visited the SK Hynix booth and wrote "Please Make More" on an HBM4E wafer display, illustrating the intensity of demand versus constrained supply.

High-bandwidth memory stacks DRAM dies vertically through microscopic copper pathways and bonds them to GPUs on silicon interposers. An HBM3E stack delivers approximately "1.2 terabytes per second," compared to conventional DDR5's 50-100 gigabytes per second. The manufacturing constraint lies partly in TSMC's CoWoS advanced packaging process, expanding from 35,000 to 120,000-130,000 monthly wafer starts by end-2026.

The deeper issue involves wafer economics. Producing HBM3E consumes roughly three to four times the wafer capacity required for equivalent DDR5 output. Industry analysts confirm wafer supply runs "more than 20 percent below demand," with three dominant suppliers—SK Hynix, Samsung, and Micron—meeting only approximately half of medium-to-long-term requirements.

Samsung unveiled HBM5 mockups featuring 2-nanometer base die manufacturing and proprietary Heat Path Block thermal management. Samsung plans mass production around 2028. SK Hynix holds approximately 57 percent of global HBM revenue as of Q3 2025, with Samsung at 22 percent and Micron at 21 percent.

Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon declared 2026 "the year of agents," projecting global AI token consumption rising from 31.7 billion tokens per ten seconds currently to 1.27 trillion by 2030—roughly a fortyfold increase. Agentic AI systems operating continuously demand far greater memory bandwidth than conversational interfaces requiring human interaction. This structural shift drives approximately $2 trillion in projected 2026 spending across hardware, software, and services.

Qualcomm announced Dragonfly, its inaugural data-center product line for AI server infrastructure, recognizing that edge device processing cannot route entirely through cloud systems at projected token volumes.

Taiwan's TAIEX index closed at record 45,557 points Tuesday, driven by AI investment momentum. Nvidia, valued at approximately $5.4 trillion, remains the world's most valuable company. SK Hynix crossed $1 trillion market capitalization for the first time last week. Goldman Sachs revised profit forecasts upward by 24 percent for SK Hynix and 23 percent for Samsung by 2028.

Nvidia debuted the Isaac GR00T Reference Humanoid Robot at GTC Taipei, featuring 75 degrees of freedom and an Nvidia Jetson AGX Thor T5000 compute module. The non-proprietary platform will see commercial availability from Unitree in late 2026. Qualcomm similarly unveiled robotics reference designs under Dragonfly branding.

The memory bottleneck constraining every AI system globally is projected to begin easing around 2030.

articles.title: Samsung shows first HBM5 mockup at Computex with Heat Path Block cooling
articles.body:
Samsung unveiled its first HBM5 (High Bandwidth Memory 5) mockup at Computex 2026 in Taipei, featuring an innovative Heat Path Block (HPB) cooling technology. The HPB design creates additional thermal pathways within the D2D PHY region, improving heat dissipation and reducing thermal resistance.

Samsung plans to use base dies manufactured on its in-house 2nm foundry process for HBM5. The memory is being prepared in 12-layer, 16-layer, and 20-layer DRAM stack configurations, with mass production expected around 2028.

The unveiling comes as Samsung seeks to narrow the gap with SK hynix, which holds approximately 57% of global HBM revenue. Both memory manufacturers are now targeting the same die-to-die hotspot challenge but employing competing in-package cooling designs — Samsung's Heat Path Block versus SK Hynix's alternative thermal management approach.

The strategic significance is high: HBM5 will support NVIDIA's post-Vera Rubin generation of AI accelerators, and securing the supply relationship is critical for Samsung's recovery in the high-margin AI memory segment. Mass production in 2028 aligns with Samsung's 2nm foundry ramp, vertically integrating compute die manufacturing with memory stacking.

articles.title: The rise of local agentic computing faces a brutal reality: rising DRAM prices — RTX Spark, Gorgon Halo chips subject to 63% DRAM contract price hike this quarter
articles.body:
DRAM prices are forecast to climb another 58% to 63% this quarter, on top of the record 90% to 95% jump from Q1 2026, threatening the viability of local AI computing devices. AMD's Gorgon Halo and Nvidia's RTX Spark — both positioned for on-device AI inference — require massive memory pools (up to 192GB) at precisely when 'memory now accounts for roughly 35% of the cost of building a PC,' according to HP statements.

The memory shortage stems from manufacturers redirecting DRAM capacity toward high-margin AI accelerator memory (HBM). As a result, SK hynix leadership projected 'the shortage will run through 2030,' despite planned capacity expansions not reaching volume production before late 2027.

The Gorgon Halo's 256-bit interface maxes out around 212 GB/s, significantly slower than competitors like Apple's M3 Ultra (819 GB/s), constraining inference speeds regardless of available capacity. Memory now accounts for roughly 35% of total PC build cost — the highest share in 15 years. The confluence of AI PC launches (AMD Gorgon Halo, NVIDIA RTX Spark) and the HBM-driven DRAM shortage creates a market paradox: chips designed to democratize AI inference are launching into their most expensive memory environment in a decade and a half.

Vendors are expanding memory configurations while maintaining premium pricing — a deliberate choice rather than market necessity. PC vendors including Lenovo, Dell, HP, Acer and ASUS have warned clients of 15-20% price hikes.

articles.title: Alphabet raises record $85B in equity for AI infrastructure
articles.body:
Alphabet upsized its equity offering to $84.75 billion on June 3, up from an initial target of $80 billion, a nearly 6% increase driven by investor appetite for AI exposure. The stock sale, which priced on June 2, shattered the previous record held by Petroleo Brasileiro's 2010 offering of $70 billion.

CEO Sundar Pichai announced that initial demand was so strong the offering was upsized from $40 billion to $45 billion in the first tranche, with a second $40 billion tranche planned for the next quarter. Berkshire Hathaway's $10 billion private placement was split evenly between Class A and Class C stock.

The company describes the capital raise as part of its "multi-year investment strategy to meet the AI opportunity ahead." Alphabet expects to spend between $180 billion and $190 billion on capital expenditure in 2026, primarily directed toward data centers and AI compute infrastructure. The company reported $109.9 billion in revenue for Q1 2026, up 22% year-on-year, with Google Cloud growing 63% to $20 billion.

The timing coincides with Anthropic's confidential IPO filing on June 1, one day prior. Both Anthropic and OpenAI are preparing public listings, with Anthropic last valued at $965 billion and targeting a valuation above $1 trillion.

Goldman Sachs estimates "$4 trillion to $8 trillion in total capital investment" will flow into AI infrastructure over the next five years. Industry observers note that unlike the dot-com era, today's AI companies are already profitable, distinguishing this investment cycle from previous speculative bubbles.

articles.title: K-온디바이스 AI 반도체 예산 8000억 확정
articles.body:
산업통상자원부가 'K-온디바이스 AI 반도체 기술개발' 사업 예산을 약 8002억 원으로 확정했다. 당초 2월 발표 1조원(정책금융 7000억원 + 수요기업 3000억원)에서 2000억원 줄어든 규모로, 정부 분담금은 약 5111억 원이며 나머지는 수요기업이 부담한다.

이 사업은 2026~2030년 5년간 자동차·IoT·가전·기계·로봇·방위산업 등에 적용 가능한 맞춤형 AI 반도체와 모듈, 소프트웨어 개발을 지원한다. 수요기업으로는 현대자동차, LG전자, 두산로보틱스, 대동, 한국항공우주산업(KAI)이 참여한다.

예산 삭감에 대해 업계에서는 사업 매력도가 낮아졌다는 우려가 나온다. 개발된 칩이 상용화에 이르지 못할 수 있다는 점, 지식재산권 노출 위험, 양산 보장 부재 등이 주요 우려 사항이다. 한 반도체 업계 관계자는 '투자 대비 효율이 크지 않다'고 전했다.

정부는 이러한 우려에 대해 실증·양산·금융지원·규제 개선 등 상용화 지원을 강화하겠다고 약속했다. 산업부 장관 김정관은 개발된 칩이 '자동차 등 주요 산업에 실제 탑재될 수 있도록' 정부가 지원하겠다고 밝혔다. 사업 착수는 당초 예정인 3월에서 약 3개월 지연되어 2026년 7월로 조정됐다.

articles.title: 구글, AI 데이터센터 전력 수요 대응 위해 발전 사업 직접 진출
articles.body:
알파벳이 AI 인프라 투자를 위해 850억 달러 규모 주식 발행을 진행 중인 가운데, 구글이 AI 데이터센터 전력 수요를 직접 해결하기 위해 발전 사업에 뛰어들었다. 한 애널리스트는 "현재 AI 인프라 경쟁에서 최대 변수는 자본이 아니라 전력"이라고 지적했다.

구글은 재생에너지 개발사 인터섹트(Intersect)를 47억5000만 달러(약 6조4000억 원)에 인수, 수 기가와트 규모의 발전 프로젝트를 확보했다. 이로써 구글은 발전 사업자를 직접 소유한 최초의 주요 빅테크 기업이 됐다.

데이터센터는 수천 대의 서버와 냉각 시스템을 가동하기 위해 막대한 전력을 필요로 하지만, 전력망 연결과 인허가 절차가 속도를 따라가지 못하는 상황이다.

구글은 추가 용량 확보를 위해 볼터스(Volters)와 동부 미국 전력망에서 최대 100메가와트 규모의 계약을 맺었으며, 피크 시간대 소비를 줄이는 수요반응 프로그램도 운영 중이다. 경쟁사들은 xAI, 오픈AI, 메타가 가스 발전 데이터센터를 구축하고, 마이크로소프트가 원자력 재가동에 투자하는 등 대체 방식을 모색하고 있다.

articles.title: 한국 정부, Anthropic '프로젝트 글래스윙' 참여…삼성·SK·KISA 동참
articles.body:
한국 정부가 Anthropic의 '프로젝트 글래스윙(Project Glasswing)' 이니셔티브를 통해 클로드 미토스(Claude Mitus)에 대한 접근권을 확보했다. 과학기술정보통신부가 한국인터넷진흥원(KISA)을 통해 참여하며, 삼성전자, SK하이닉스, SK텔레콤 등 주요 기업도 동참한다.

Anthropic은 프로젝트 글래스윙 참여를 15개국, 약 150개 신규 기관으로 확대했다. 유럽연합 국가 중 프랑스, 독일, 이탈리아, 네덜란드, 벨기에, 스웨덴이 포함됐다.

이번 확대는 기존에 다루지 않았던 분야인 '전력, 수도, 의료, 통신, 하드웨어' 인프라 산업까지 범위를 넓혔다. 프로젝트 글래스윙은 AI 모델이 사이버보안 취약점을 발견하거나 악의적으로 활용될 가능성을 정부 및 주요 기관과 공동으로 검토하는 이니셔티브다. 한국의 참여는 AI 시스템의 국가 핵심 인프라 보안 리스크를 사전에 평가한다는 의미를 가진다.

articles.title: Microsoft unveils Project Solara AI, a chip-to-cloud platform built to power a new generation of 'agent-first' enterprise devices
articles.body:
Microsoft announced Project Solara at Build 2026, describing it as 'a chip-to-cloud platform built to power a new generation of agent-first enterprise devices.' Rather than running traditional applications, these devices function as interfaces to AI agents hosted in Microsoft's cloud infrastructure.

The platform features the Microsoft Device Ecosystem Platform (MDEP), a lightweight edge operating system uniquely built on Android's open-source codebase rather than Windows. According to Steven Bathiche, Microsoft's Corporate Vice President, 'The operating system is liminal, transcending the device and the cloud.'

Microsoft partnered with Qualcomm and MediaTek for silicon, offering reference designs for manufacturers rather than producing devices directly. Two concept devices were unveiled: a desk-mounted AI hub using MediaTek IoT chips and a wearable badge powered by Qualcomm hardware. Both devices integrate cameras, microphones, and connectivity features to support cloud-connected AI agent functionality.

Project Solara represents Microsoft's answer to what the company calls the 'next computer' — an agent-first platform that dissolves the boundary between edge device and cloud. By building on AOSP rather than Windows, Microsoft signals a willingness to bypass its legacy OS for new form factors where AI agent orchestration is the primary function.

articles.title: Trump signs AI executive order seeking 30-day government access to frontier models before release
articles.body:
President Trump signed an executive order establishing a voluntary framework granting federal agencies 30-day early access to frontier AI models before public release. The order involves the NSA, CISA, and NIST creating a classified benchmark that decides which systems qualify as a 'covered frontier model.'

Key provisions include: Voluntary participation with no mandatory licensing or pre-clearance requirements; a classified threshold that agencies will determine which models require review; an AI cybersecurity clearinghouse coordinating vulnerability detection and patching; and critical infrastructure protection supporting sectors like rural hospitals and community banks.

The order represents a scaled-back approach from an earlier 90-day draft the administration abandoned. It was prompted partly by Anthropic's Claude Mythos identifying thousands of zero-day vulnerabilities across major systems, signaling government interest in security vetting of advanced AI capabilities. Section three states that nothing in it authorizes mandatory government licensing, pre-clearance, or permitting for new models, including frontier models. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth urged the timeline reduction during a June 1 meeting.

articles.title: 트럼프, AI '사전 검토' 행정명령 서명...90일서 30일로 축소
articles.body:
도널드 트럼프 미국 대통령이 6월 2일(현지시간) 프론티어 AI 모델에 대한 정부의 30일 사전 검토 시스템을 도입하는 행정명령에 서명했다. 첨단 AI를 개발하는 기업들은 자발적으로 보안 평가를 위한 정보와 접근권을 제공해야 하며, 의무적 라이선스나 사전 승인은 아니다.

초안에서는 최대 90일의 검토 기간을 제안했으나, AI 업계의 반발로 14일 주장을 거쳐 30일로 조율됐다. 트럼프는 AI의 경제적 혜택을 훼손하고 중국 대비 미국 경쟁력을 약화시킬 수 있다는 우려로 서명을 주저했지만, AI 자문관 데이빗 삭스가 의무적 규제가 될 수 있다고 설득한 것으로 전해진다.

이 조치는 앤트로픽의 '미소스(Misos)'와 같은 고성능 모델이 국가 안보를 위협하는 사이버 공격에 악용될 수 있다는 우려를 반영한다. 마이클 크라트시오스 백악관 과학기술정책국장은 "이 명령은 미국이 AI 분야에서 리더십을 유지하는 동시에 사이버 방어를 강화하는 데 도움이 된다"고 밝혔다.

articles.title: MS, 기업 전용 자체 모델 7종 공개...앤트로픽과 격차 좁혔다
articles.body:
마이크로소프트(MS)가 빌드 개발자 콘퍼런스에서 추론, 코딩, 이미지 생성, 음성 등 분야를 아우르는 7종의 자체 MAI(Microsoft AI) 모델을 공개했다.

주요 모델: MAI-Thinking-1(350억 활성 파라미터 플래그십 추론 모델, AIME 2025 수학 벤치마크 97%); MAI-Code-1-Flash(GitHub Copilot 최적화 경량 코딩 모델); MAI-Image-2.5 & Flash(텍스트-이미지 생성 및 편집); MAI-Transcribe-1.5(43개 언어 음성 인식); MAI-Voice-2(15개 언어 자연 음성 합성); Aion 시리즈(Windows PC 배포용 경량 모델).

핵심 기술은 '프런티어 튜닝(Frontier Tuning)'으로, 기업이 프라이빗 환경에서 자체 데이터로 AI 모델을 맞춤화할 수 있는 강화학습 기술이다. MS는 튜닝된 MAI 모델이 GPT-5.4 수준의 성능을 내면서도 10배 높은 효율과 최대 90%의 비용 절감을 달성한다고 시연했다.

이 전략은 MS의 오픈AI 및 앤트로픽 의존도를 낮추면서, 애저(Azure)를 경쟁력 있는 AI 플랫폼으로 포지셔닝하는 효과를 낸다. 사티아 나델라 CEO는 "기업들이 이제 AI 생태계에 단순 소비자가 아닌 직접 참여자로 나설 수 있게 됐다"고 밝혔다.

articles.title: MS, 상시 실행형 AI 비서 '스카우트' 발표
articles.body:
마이크로소프트(MS)가 샌프란시스코 빌드 개발자 콘퍼런스에서 상시 실행형 AI 비서 '스카우트(Scout)'를 발표했다. 스카우트는 단순 챗봇을 넘어 이메일, 일정 관리, 문서 관리를 담당하는 자율 AI 에이전트로, 독립적인 정체성을 가지고 있다.

스카우트는 독립형 앱이자 MS의 개편된 코파일럿 슈퍼앱의 기본 자동 조종 에이전트로 작동한다. 내부 코드명 '프로젝트 로브스터(Project Lobster)'로 개발됐으며, 오픈소스 플랫폼 OpenClaw에서 보안 우려가 제기된 교훈을 바탕으로 기업 환경에 맞게 설계됐다.

스카우트의 차별점은 이메일 시스템과 캘린더에서 독립적인 디지털 팀원으로 기능한다는 것이다. 스카우트는 회의 변경 요청, 의제 작성, 알림, 리소스 준비 등을 처리하며 '워크 IQ(Work IQ)' 프레임워크를 통해 사용자 업무 패턴을 학습한다. 보안 강화를 위해 MS Entra 독립 신원, MS Purview 정보 보호가 실시간 적용되며 모든 검증 과정이 감사 로그에 기록된다.

스카우트는 현재 MS의 실험적 '프런티어(Frontier)' 프로그램을 통해 제한적 프라이빗 미리보기 상태이며, GitHub Copilot 라이선스 보유자를 대상으로 초기 버전이 제공된다.

articles.title: MS, AI로 설계한 양자 칩 '마요라나 2' 공개
articles.body:
마이크로소프트(MS)가 AI 지원으로 설계한 차세대 양자컴퓨팅 칩 '마요라나 2(Majorana 2)'를 공개하고 2029년 상용화를 목표로 제시했다.

MS는 6월 2일(미국 시간) 샌프란시스코 빌드 개발자 콘퍼런스에서 마요라나 2를 발표했다. 이 칩은 MS의 과학·공학 연구 에이전트 시스템인 '디스커버리(Discovery)' AI 플랫폼을 활용한 최초의 주요 하드웨어 사례다.

주요 재료 변경: 마요라나 1에서 사용하던 알루미늄 초전도체를 납(Lead)으로 교체하고, 반도체 활성 영역을 인듐비화물(InAs)과 인듐비화안티몬(InAsSb) 조합으로 전환했다.

성능 향상: 양자 정보가 저장되는 위상학적 갭이 전 세대 대비 2배 이상 확장되어 외부 노이즈와 오류로부터 큐비트를 보호한다. 큐비트 안정성이 1000배 이상 향상됐다(마요라나 1 1~12밀리초 → 마요라나 2 평균 20초 이상, 일부는 1분 초과). 큐비트 수도 8개에서 12개로 확대됐다.

AI의 역할: Discovery AI가 새 재료 조합 및 제조 공정을 탐색하고, 이전에는 수 주가 걸리던 큐비트 측정을 자동화했다. 납은 물에 녹아 표준 반도체 공정에서 제조 난제를 안겨줬는데, Discovery AI가 이 문제 해결을 지원했다.

마요라나 2는 양자컴퓨팅 기술 가속과 에이전틱 AI 활용 가능성을 동시에 보여주는 사례로 주목받고 있다.

articles.title: Microsoft's Majorana 2 quantum chip is also a case study for agentic AI in R&D
articles.body:
Microsoft announced its Majorana 2 quantum chip alongside the general availability of Microsoft Discovery, an agentic AI platform for scientific research and development. The quantum chip demonstrates the practical application of agentic AI in hardware design.

Majorana 2 achieves remarkable reliability improvements: qubits are 1,000 times more reliable than first-generation models; mean qubit lifetime of 20 seconds (compared to industry standard microseconds); revised roadmap targeting commercial scalability by 2029.

Contrary to assumptions that AI designed the chip, the contribution was more nuanced. The critical decision to switch from aluminum to lead superconducting material came from conventional materials research. Instead, the AI platform managed fabrication workflows, automated measurements that previously required weeks, synthesized nearly two decades of siloed research data, and surfaced correlations humans couldn't identify across large datasets.

A concrete success involved automating qubit measurements — detecting quantum states by analyzing electron numbers on semiconductor wires. What previously 'takes weeks' now happens through agentic automation handling 'parallel voltage adjustments in hundreds of parameters simultaneously.'

Microsoft Discovery is now available to enterprise customers with security and governance features, plus a free preview app for GitHub Copilot users.

articles.title: Qualcomm Announces Dragonfly Brand for Data Center Products, More Info to Come June 24th
articles.body:
Qualcomm unveiled 'Dragonfly,' a new brand designation for its upcoming data center products, during CEO Cristiano Amon's Computex keynote presentation. The announcement served as a teaser for more comprehensive details promised at Qualcomm's June 24th investor day event.

The company stated: 'The compute continuum is complete. Introducing Qualcomm Dragonfly.' This branding effort represents Qualcomm's strategic push to establish itself as a significant data center processor manufacturer, leveraging its Oryon CPU cores and Hexagon NPU technologies.

Qualcomm is developing both server-grade CPUs and AI accelerators for this market. The AI200 accelerator is scheduled for release later in 2026, followed by AI250 models in 2027, described as 'much more ambitious rack-scale products.' The accelerators are expected to cut power usage by 35% to 70% compared with conventional GPUs while delivering improved inference performance.

Qualcomm did not disclose specific Dragonfly product specifications during the event. CEO Amon declared 2026 the 'Year of the Agent,' noting that global AI token consumption currently runs at 31.7 billion tokens every ten seconds and is projected to reach 1.27 trillion tokens by 2030. Dragonfly joins Qualcomm's existing product families including Snapdragon SoCs and the Dragonwing brand for IoT and robotics.

articles.title: Cisco Preps For A World Of AI Agent Coworkers, Frontier Model Threats
articles.body:
Cisco is preparing enterprise infrastructure for an emerging landscape where AI agents function as autonomous coworkers, while confronting security risks posed by frontier AI models capable of rapidly identifying and exploiting vulnerabilities.

At Cisco Live 2026, the company unveiled its AgenticOps platform and expanded AI infrastructure capabilities. According to DJ Sampath, senior vice president and general manager of Cisco's AI Software and Platform Group, this positions Cisco uniquely due to its ability to 'manufacture our own silicon' and create 'a co-designed full stack that goes all the way from silicon to the network to the security.'

A critical challenge emerges from AI agents' operational impact. Cisco's research found that 'agents generated 450 percent more traffic per task' compared to traditional tools. Additionally, frontier models like Anthropic's Claude Mythos Preview dramatically accelerate vulnerability detection — Project Glasswing uncovered 'more than 10,000 vulnerabilities' within a month.

Cisco introduced Live Protect, described as a 'digital immune system' for shielding hardware from newly discovered flaws during patching cycles. The platform will expand across switches, firewalls, and routers, with post-quantum cryptography support arriving this summer.

Foundational offerings include Cisco Cloud Control with AI Canvas, Agent Builder, and App Builder, enabling human-agent collaboration and custom workflow development through natural language interfaces.

articles.title: Astera Labs showcases 320-lane PCIe 6.0 switch for vendor-agnostic scaling in data centers
articles.body:
Astera Labs demonstrated its Scorpio X-Series 320-lane PCIe 6.0 switch at Computex 2026, positioning it as 'the industry's largest open memory-semantic fabric switch.' The device delivers significant improvements over previous generations.

Performance Specifications: 320 PCIe 6.0 lanes (up from 144 in prior models); 20 Tbps switching bandwidth (previously 9 Tbps); supports up to 80 accelerators per switch, compared to 32 with older technology.

Practical Benefits: The new architecture 'reduces switch hops from as many as three to one and cuts switch count by a factor of four to six' for large clusters while maintaining comprehensive connectivity.

Advanced Features: The switch includes Hypercast, a hardware-based data replication engine addressing multicast traffic challenges in AI models, plus in-network compute capabilities that can 'reduce communication latency by more than 50% in certain workloads.'

Market Availability: Production ramp is scheduled for the second half of 2026, with current sampling underway among leading hyperscalers.

The vendor-agnostic design works with any accelerators using standard PCIe connectivity, including AMD and Nvidia solutions. Unlike proprietary scale-up interconnects (NVLink, UALink), Scorpio X uses open PCIe 6.0, enabling heterogeneous GPU cluster deployment without vendor lock-in.

articles.title: Github Copilot customers report up to 100-fold price hikes — AI sticker shock bites as Microsoft switches to usage-based pricing
articles.body:
Microsoft has transitioned GitHub Copilot from flat-rate pricing to usage-based billing, triggering significant customer backlash as some users face up to 100-fold price increases under the new model. GitHub announced that all Copilot plans transitioned to usage-based billing on June 1, 2026.

Instead of counting premium requests, every Copilot plan now includes a monthly allotment of GitHub AI Credits, with the option for paid plans to purchase additional usage. Usage is calculated based on token consumption, including input, output, and cached tokens, using the listed API rates for each model.

Copilot Pro remains $10/month, Pro+ remains $39/month, Business remains $19/user/month, and Enterprise remains $39/user/month. However, the shift to token-based billing has left many users facing bills far exceeding previous subscription costs.

One user reported that 'in a single normal development day I've already used around 360 AI credits,' projecting monthly usage would greatly exceed included credits without heavy usage patterns. This connects to the broader 'token-maxing' phenomenon where AI coding agents consume far more compute than simple completion tools. The price shock also echoes Uber's simultaneous announcement of a $1,500/month cap on Claude Code spending per employee.

articles.title: Korean tech workers splash cash on luxury brands after bumper bonus payouts — luxury goods sales rocket nearly 150% in Gyeonggi Province semiconductor belt
articles.body:
South Korean semiconductor workers have dramatically increased spending on luxury goods following substantial bonus payouts. In Gyeonggi Province's semiconductor hub, luxury jewelry sales surged 146.3% at one department store, while luxury watches climbed 85.3%.

The Chosun Daily reports that department stores across the region experienced significant boosts: Lotte Department Store Dongtan Branch saw overall luxury sales rise 40% year-over-year through late May, while The Hyundai Department Store's Pangyo location recorded a 46.1% increase in May alone — well above the 32% national average for Hyundai stores.

Department store representatives attribute the consumption spike to 'the boom in semiconductor companies, the creation of advanced industrial clusters, and the move-in of new large apartment complexes.' Premium European brands including Rolex, Cartier, Hermès, and Chanel are benefiting substantially from this spending wave among newly affluent tech workers.

The Samsung Electronics union ratification of a deal allocating 10.5% of semiconductor operating profit as special bonuses — averting an 18-day strike — triggered a major surge in worker compensation. This bonus cycle, combined with SK Hynix's record performance-linked pay, has created one of the largest semiconductor worker income events in Korean history.

articles.title: 우버, '클로드 코드' 과다 지출에 제동...월 한도 230만원
articles.body:
차량 공유 서비스 기업 우버(Uber)가 최근 직원들의 AI 도구 사용에 제한을 뒀다. 블룸버그 보도에 따르면 우버는 직원 1인당 AI 코딩 도구 사용을 월 1,500달러(약 230만원)로 상한선을 설정했다.

이 제한은 Anthropic의 '클로드 코드(Claude Code)', Cursor 등 코딩 에이전트에만 적용되며 다른 도구 예산은 영향을 받지 않는다. 이에 따라 모든 직원에게 AI 도구 사용량 모니터링 대시보드가 제공되고, 사용 한도 초과 시 승인 요청 절차가 마련됐다.

우버는 이를 에이전틱 AI 도입과 실험을 책임감 있게 장려하기 위한 단순한 접근 방식이라고 밝혔다. 지난 4월 우버 CTO 프라빈 나쿨리는 연간 AI 예산을 이미 소진했다고 밝혔고, CEO 다라 코스로샤히는 회사 코드의 약 10%가 AI 에이전트에 의해 생성되고 있다고 언급했다.

'토큰 맥시마이징(Token-maxing)' 현상 — 생산성 극대화를 위해 AI 토큰 사용을 최대화하는 현상 — 으로 일부 기업들이 비용 통제에 나서고 있다. 월마트도 내부 AI 에이전트의 직원 사용 시간을 제한했다고 전해진다.

articles.title: 모델 라우팅 넘어 실행 위치까지 자동 배분...퍼플렉시티 하이브리드 추론
articles.body:
퍼플렉시티(Perplexity)가 컴퓨텍스 2026에서 AI 태스크를 개인 PC와 클라우드 서버 사이에서 자동으로 분배하는 '하이브리드 인퍼런스 오케스트레이터(Hybrid Inference Orchestrator)'를 발표했다. 기존 모델 라우팅이 소형·대형 모델 선택에 그쳤던 것과 달리, 이 시스템은 데이터 보안 수준과 로컬 하드웨어 역량을 실시간으로 평가하여 물리적 실행 위치를 결정한다.

시연에서는 기밀 계약서를 분석할 때 민감한 재무 정보를 사용자의 PC에서 로컬로 처리하고, 복잡한 추론 태스크만 암호화하여 클라우드로 전송하는 방식이 시연됐다. 오프라인 상태에서도 로컬 모델을 사용해 기능을 유지한다.

CEO 아라빈드 스리니바스는 'AI 시대의 핵심 경쟁 우위는 특정 모델 성능을 넘어서 모델과 하드웨어 자원을 가장 효율적으로 연결하는 오케스트레이션 레이어에 있다'고 강조했다.

이 기술은 인프라 비용 압박과 글로벌 데이터센터 전력 부족 문제를 분산 컴퓨팅으로 해결하며, 금융·의료·방위·법률 등 엄격한 데이터 보호 요건을 가진 산업이 주요 타깃 시장이다.

articles.title: Intel launches Xeon 6+ CPU, pitches it for agentic AI boom
articles.body:
Intel launched its Xeon 6+ processor family (codenamed Clearwater Forest) at Computex 2026, marking the world's first datacenter processor built on Intel's 18A process technology — often referred to as a 1.8nm-class manufacturing node.

The flagship Xeon 6990E+ packs 288 Darkmont efficiency cores into a single socket, with 576 MB of last-level cache, 12-channel DDR5 memory at 8000 MT/s, 96 PCIe 5.0 lanes, 64 CXL 2.0 lanes, and a TDP from 330W to 450W. The Clearwater Forest chips use twelve separate compute tiles fabbed on Intel's 18A process, resting upon three active base tiles, with twelve EMIB tiles connecting everything via Foveros Direct technology.

Intel is pitching Xeon 6+ for the agentic AI era, noting that inference and agentic workloads are shifting requirements away from GPU-heavy training toward high-concurrency CPU orchestration. A single liquid-cooled rack can support up to 36,864 Xeon 6+ cores in a dense compute configuration designed to maximize AI agent concurrency within an approximate 100 kW rack power envelope.

The processor is available immediately through Dell Technologies, HPE, Lenovo, and Supermicro. Next-gen Xeon 7 'Diamond Rapids' CPUs will launch in 2027 on the Intel 18A-P process.

Intel also announced rackscale AI infrastructure in collaboration with SambaNova (SN-50 RDUs) and Foxconn for system integration, targeting inference and agentic workloads. Separately, Vista Equity Partners and Cambium Capital launched Vector Core Compute, an inference neocloud running Intel Xeon processors, SambaNova RDUs, and NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs.

articles.title: Marvell Announces Availability of Industry's First 102.4 Tbps Switch Purpose-Built for AI and Cloud Data Center Infrastructure
articles.body:
Marvell Technology announced the Teralynx T100, the industry's first 102.4 Tbps switch silicon purpose-built for the AI era. The T100 was architected from the ground up for AI — enabling the industry's lowest power consumption and lowest latency at this bandwidth tier to address critical bottlenecks in today's large AI clusters.

Key specifications: operates under 1,000W (25% lower power than competing solutions); supports 512-port scale-out radix; flexible scale-up fabric protocols; advanced 3nm process technology with monolithic design; multiple deployment options including ball grid array, co-packaged copper, and co-packaged optics.

The T100 supports both scale-out deployments for large training clusters and scale-up deployments with emerging standards like Ethernet Scale-Up Networking (ESUN) and Ultra Ethernet Consortium (UEC) requirements. Sampling to customers began in Q2 2026.

Rishi Chugh, VP and GM of Marvell's Data Center Switch Business Unit, noted the device was 'designed without the legacy baggage that inflates power' while delivering performance needed for next-generation infrastructure.

articles.title: NVIDIA and TSMC Bring AI Into Fabs to Advance Semiconductor Design and Manufacturing
articles.body:
NVIDIA announced that TSMC, the world's leading semiconductor company, is using NVIDIA accelerated computing and AI to advance semiconductor design and manufacturing at NVIDIA GTC Taipei. The collaboration covers the entire semiconductor design and manufacturing lifecycle.

Key applications: TSMC is using NVIDIA cuLitho, a GPU-accelerated library for lithography, which delivers 20% to 50% improvement in cost effectiveness or cycle time; NVIDIA Metropolis with NVIDIA Tao toolkit for defect classification using vision AI to find chip defects at nanometer scale; TSMC is exploring NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to build a FabTwin, or a virtual fab environment for evaluating process tools and simulation workflows.

This collaboration announced by Jensen Huang at GTC Taipei represents a significant expansion of NVIDIA's role from chip supplier to AI enabler within semiconductor manufacturing itself — embedding NVIDIA compute and software into TSMC's fab operations for computational lithography, transistor simulation, defect inspection, and factory scheduling.

articles.title: Jensen Huang hosts Korea Partner Night in Taipei; eyes Korea visit June 4-5
articles.body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang hosted a 'Korea Partner Night' dinner in Taipei on June 1, bringing together approximately 100 officials from more than 30 Korean companies that partner with Nvidia. This marked the first dedicated event for Korean partners during a Computex visit.

Attendees included SK Hynix CEO Kwak Noh-jung, Samsung Electronics Memory Business VP Kim Jae-jun, LG Science Park VP Jeong Su-heon, Doosan Robotics CEO Kim Min-pyo, and Naver Cloud CEO Kim Yu-won.

Huang emphasized Korea's critical importance: 'Korea is a critical part of our ecosystem.' He expressed affection for Korean food, saying he hoped to visit chicken, samgyetang, and samgyeopsal restaurants during his upcoming Seoul visit.

After completing the Computex Taiwan schedule, Huang is set to arrive in Korea on June 4 evening, with meetings scheduled from June 5. He is expected to meet SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won, LG Group Chairman Koo Kwang-mo, Hyundai Motor Group Chairman Chung Euisun, and Naver Chairman Lee Hae-jin.

At Computex, Huang confirmed Vera Rubin is in full production, naming Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron as HBM4 suppliers — critical context for the Korea meetings. Samsung stock jumped nearly 10% on June 1 as markets priced in the visit.

Investment context: Several South Korea-focused ETFs have significantly outperformed Nvidia year-to-date, with the iShares MSCI South Korea ETF (EWY) up 111.72% compared to Nvidia's +35.51%.

articles.title: Google Gemma 4 12B: encoder-free multimodal model that runs locally on 16GB laptop
articles.body:
Google introduced Gemma 4 12B, its latest model designed to bring agentic multimodal intelligence directly to laptops. It bridges the gap between the edge-friendly E4B and the more advanced 26B Mixture of Experts (MoE), packaging powerful capabilities inside a reduced memory footprint.

Unified, encoder-free architecture: The model features a novel unified architecture with no multimodal encoders, where vision and audio inputs flow directly into the LLM backbone. The vision encoder was replaced with a lightweight embedding module (single matrix multiplication, positional embedding, normalizations), while the audio encoder was removed entirely — raw audio signals projected into the same dimensional space as text tokens.

Local deployment: small enough to run locally with just 16GB of VRAM or unified memory. Performance: nearing the larger 26B MoE model on standard benchmarks at less than half the memory footprint. Gemma 4 12B is Google's first mid-sized model to feature native audio inputs, handling text, images, audio, and video natively. Released under Apache 2.0 license.

articles.title: Computex 2026 Day Two Wrap-Up: Intel atones for Arrow Lake, Wi-Fi 8 comes into focus
articles.body:
Computex 2026 Day Two (June 3) saw Intel showcasing Xeon 6+ for data centers and AI inference, alongside multiple consumer chip and PC announcements. Intel's Clearwater Forest Xeon 6+ was the biggest server/datacenter news of the day — 288 E-cores on Intel 18A process, available immediately through major OEM partners.

AMD executives also reacted to Nvidia's RTX Spark announcement, with AMD pushing back on Nvidia's foray into the laptop CPU market: 'You're just wrong if you don't get a Strix Halo notebook.' AMD's Ryzen AI Max PRO 400 (Gorgon Halo) with up to 192GB unified memory is AMD's own on-device AI answer.

DRAM prices hit a 15-year high with 32GB of DDR5 now costing $375 minimum — a new data point in the AI-driven memory shortage crisis. Both AMD Gorgon Halo and Nvidia RTX Spark on-device AI PC platforms launch into this memory crunch.

Noctua showed an improved thermosiphon prototype targeting Q3 2027 launch. Wi-Fi 8 technology specifications were clarified across multiple vendor announcements.

articles.title: Intel Launches 1.8nm Xeon 6+ and AI Infrastructure Stack at Computex 2026
articles.body:
Intel announced Xeon 6+ processors (Clearwater Forest) at Computex 2026 — the world's first data center CPUs built on Intel's 18A (1.8nm-class) process technology. The flagship Xeon 6990E+ features 288 Darkmont efficiency cores, 576MB L3 cache, 12-channel DDR5, and 96 PCIe 5.0 lanes.

Intel is positioning Xeon 6+ for the agentic AI era: the rise of inference and agentic workloads shifts requirements from GPU training to high-concurrency CPU orchestration. A single liquid-cooled rack supports up to 36,864 cores, maximizing AI agent concurrency within ~100 kW.

AI infrastructure stack: Intel announced rackscale AI infrastructure with SambaNova (SN-50 RDUs) and Foxconn system integration. Vista Equity Partners and Cambium Capital launched Vector Core Compute — an inference neocloud using Intel Xeon, SambaNova RDUs, and NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs. Intel also previewed the E835 Ethernet solution for AI cluster networking and Crescent Island datacenter GPU for 2027.

Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said data centers will be '80% x86' through 2030, expressing confidence in CPU centrality for the agentic AI era despite growing ARM and RISC-V challengers.

articles.title: Jensen Huang says Seoul National University visit scheduled June 8
articles.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is scheduled to visit Seoul National University on June 8 during his Korea trip, according to Seoul Economic Daily. Huang arrives in Korea on June 4 evening after completing the GTC Taipei and Computex schedule. His full Korea itinerary includes meetings with SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won, LG Group Chairman Koo Kwang-mo, Hyundai Motor Group Chairman Chung Euisun, and Naver Chairman Lee Hae-jin. The Seoul National University visit on June 8 has been confirmed separately. Naver's headquarters visit is also likely during the June 8 period. Huang previously visited Korea in November 2025, approximately seven months ago. The visit follows his Korea Partner Night dinner in Taipei on June 1 where he met executives from 30+ Korean companies including Samsung, SK Hynix, LG, Doosan Robotics, and Naver. Samsung stock hit a record high on June 1 as markets priced in HBM4 supplier confirmation and the upcoming visit's partnership implications.

articles.title: EdgeConneX files to build two 730,000 sq ft data centers in Bastrop County, Texas
articles.body: EdgeConneX has filed plans to build two large-scale data center facilities in Bastrop County, Texas, each approximately 730,000 square feet. The filings represent a significant expansion of AI-focused data center capacity in the Austin-area tech corridor. Bastrop County has emerged as a key data center destination due to available land, power access, and proximity to Austin's tech ecosystem. The two facilities together would total approximately 1.46 million square feet of data center space. No timeline or power capacity figures were disclosed in the filings.

articles.title: Core42 expands AI cluster by 42MW in Buffalo, New York
articles.body: Core42, the UAE-based AI infrastructure company backed by G42, has expanded its AI compute cluster in Buffalo, New York by 42 megawatts. The expansion adds significant GPU compute capacity to Core42's North American footprint. The Buffalo facility is part of Core42's strategy to build AI infrastructure capacity outside the Middle East, serving US-based AI workloads. G42 has been expanding globally as part of a partnership with Microsoft and other major technology companies to deliver AI infrastructure at scale.

articles.title: Amazon plans nine-building data center campus in Wheatfield, Indiana
articles.body: Amazon Web Services plans to build a nine-building data center campus in Wheatfield, Indiana, according to planning documents filed with local authorities. The campus would represent a major investment in Midwest US data center capacity as hyperscalers continue aggressive buildouts to support AI infrastructure demand. Indiana has become increasingly attractive for data center investment due to available land, power infrastructure, and favorable regulatory environment. No specific power capacity or investment figure was disclosed in the planning filings.

articles.title: Google signs 100MW Bring Your Own Capacity agreement with Voltus
articles.body: Google has signed a 100 megawatt 'Bring Your Own Capacity' (BYOC) demand response agreement with Voltus, a distributed energy resource management company. The deal allows Google to dynamically reduce data center power consumption during peak grid demand periods, earning grid services revenue while supporting grid stability. BYOC agreements represent a new model for hyperscalers to contribute to grid flexibility while managing their massive electricity consumption. The 100MW agreement is one of the largest demand response commitments by a technology company. This connects to Google's broader strategy of directly acquiring power generation assets (Intersect Power acquisition for $4.75B) and managing its energy footprint across multiple approaches.

articles.title: Lambda offers glimpse into Nvidia's CPO switch, enabling 'more tokens' through substantial power savings
articles.body:
Cloud infrastructure company Lambda demonstrated Nvidia's upcoming Quantum-X Q3450-LD co-packaged optics (CPO) switch, highlighting significant efficiency advantages for large-scale GPU clusters. The liquid-cooled switch features 144 x 800G ports delivering 115.2 terabits per second of non-blocking capacity in a 4U form factor. Unlike traditional switches requiring 72 separate transceivers consuming 25 watts each, CPO integration eliminates this power overhead.

Rich Underwood, Lambda's HPC systems architect, explained: 'All of that power saving equals more efficient GPU and compute time, and more compute time equals more tokens.' For a hypothetical 128,000-GPU cluster, CPO reduces laser requirements from 5 million to 1 million units, directly translating to increased computational capacity.

Nvidia's networking division confirmed both photonics and copper technologies will coexist in future architectures, with copper remaining optimal for short-distance interconnects where passive, zero-power solutions suffice. NVIDIA's Spectrum-X Ethernet Photonics (CPO-based) is now in full-scale production as of mid-2026.

articles.title: Vista Equity Partners launches Vector Core Compute, an inference 'agentic neocloud' with SambaNova and Intel compute
articles.body:
Vista Equity Partners and Cambium Capital have launched Vector Core Compute, a new purpose-built enterprise inference cloud running Intel Xeon processors, SambaNova SN-50 Reconfigurable Dataflow Units (RDUs), and NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs. The companies plan to use new rackscale AI infrastructure from Intel, Nvidia, and SambaNova to offer customers fully disaggregated inference via a new inference cloud offering.

SambaNova's SN-50 RDU provides a heterogeneous alternative to pure-GPU inference stacks, with its reconfigurable dataflow architecture targeting token throughput and latency efficiency for LLM serving. Intel Xeon 6+ provides the orchestration CPU layer, handling agentic workflow routing and agent concurrency at scale.

This represents a significant validation of the Intel-SambaNova partnership announced at Computex 2026, and positions SambaNova's SN-50 as a production component in enterprise inference infrastructure alongside Nvidia Blackwell.

articles.title: IBM announces five-year, $10bn quantum investment
articles.body: IBM has announced a five-year, $10 billion investment in quantum computing, reaffirming its commitment to being a leader in the emerging technology. The investment covers quantum hardware development, quantum software and algorithms, and quantum networking infrastructure. IBM has been one of the most consistent investors in quantum computing, with its IBM Quantum Network spanning hundreds of partners globally. The announcement comes as Microsoft unveiled its Majorana 2 quantum chip, targeting 2029 commercial scalability — the same timeline IBM is targeting. The $10 billion commitment signals that quantum computing is transitioning from research to infrastructure investment, with hyperscalers and enterprise IT vendors accelerating timelines.

articles.title: Micron in High-Volume Production of HBM4 Designed for NVIDIA Vera Rubin, PCIe Gen6 SSD and SOCAMM2
articles.body:
Micron announced at Computex 2026 that its HBM4 36GB 12H is in high-volume production, designed for NVIDIA's Vera Rubin platform. The HBM4 delivers greater than 2.8 TB/s bandwidth and 20% better power efficiency compared to HBM3E, enabling a 2.6x increase in LLM inference throughput (tokens per second for every 2x bandwidth increase).

Micron also announced the industry's first PCIe Gen6 SSD in high-volume production — the Micron 9650. It delivers up to 2x the read performance of Gen5 with 100% higher performance per watt, supporting up to 28 GB/s sequential read throughput and 5.5 million random read IOPS. Optimized for agentic AI workloads and liquid-cooled environments.

Additionally, Micron showcased its 192GB SOCAMM2 memory module for NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform — a next-generation compute express link memory format enabling higher capacity and bandwidth for AI training and inference systems.

The three product announcements position Micron as a full-stack AI memory supplier across GPU (HBM4), CPU (SOCAMM2/DDR5), and storage (PCIe Gen6 SSD) layers — a vertically comprehensive AI infrastructure memory portfolio.

articles.title: AMD executives react to Nvidia's RTX Spark: 'You're just wrong if you don't get a Strix Halo notebook'
articles.body:
AMD executives responded directly to Nvidia's RTX Spark laptop AI chip announcement at Computex 2026, aggressively defending their Ryzen AI Max PRO 400 (Gorgon Halo) platform. An AMD executive stated: 'You're just wrong if you don't get a Strix Halo notebook.' The Gorgon Halo offers up to 192GB of unified memory for on-device AI inference, compared to the shared memory architecture of Nvidia's RTX Spark system.

The competitive dynamic is significant: Nvidia's RTX Spark marks its first entry into the laptop CPU/SoC market, directly challenging AMD's Ryzen AI franchise. AMD counters that its Strix Halo platform offers superior memory bandwidth and capacity for AI workloads at a given price point.

The memory debate is complicated by the DRAM price crisis: 32GB of DDR5 now costs $375 minimum (up from ~$90 pre-AI memory shortage), making the 192GB Gorgon Halo configurations significantly more expensive to build. Both AMD and Nvidia are launching on-device AI platforms into the most expensive memory environment in 15 years.

articles.title: TSMC 3nm price hikes of up to 15% in H2 2026 as AI demand tightens foundry capacity
articles.body:
TSMC is implementing 3 nanometer process price hikes of up to 15% in the second half of 2026, underscoring how central TSMC is to the AI chip supply chain for Nvidia, AMD, Google, AWS and others. The price increases reflect TSMC's dominant position in advanced node manufacturing and the insatiable demand from AI chip developers.

Context: TSMC's CoWoS advanced packaging capacity is expanding from 35,000 to 120,000-130,000 monthly wafer starts by end-2026, but remains constrained relative to demand. The 3nm node hosts some of the most critical AI chips including NVIDIA's Blackwell/Vera Rubin GPUs, Apple's A18 series, and AMD's EPYC Venice (2nm). Price hikes at TSMC propagate directly to AI infrastructure costs downstream.

The price increase signals TSMC's confidence in its monopoly-like position at the advanced node frontier and its ability to pass rising packaging and substrate costs through to customers. NVIDIA and AMD have already built TSMC pricing into their product roadmaps through long-term supply agreements.

articles.title: UCAR wins injunction against US gov't's attempts to transition management of Wyoming supercomputing center
articles.body: The University Corporation for Atmospheric Research (UCAR) has won an injunction against the US government's attempts to transition management of the NCAR-Wyoming Supercomputing Center. The legal win temporarily blocks the Department of Energy's efforts to hand management of the facility to a different entity. The supercomputing center hosts the Derecho supercomputer, one of the most powerful research computing systems in the US, used for atmospheric science and climate modeling. The injunction represents a significant legal challenge to the current administration's plan to restructure federal research computing infrastructure. DOGE-era budget and personnel cuts had been targeting research computing institutions, making this legal victory significant for the scientific computing community.

articles.title: CoolIT designs 15kW coldplate to future-proof liquid cooling for GPUs
articles.body: CoolIT Systems has designed a 15 kilowatt coldplate capable of handling the thermal output of next-generation AI accelerators. The design targets GPU racks approaching and exceeding 120 kW per rack — the thermal density anticipated for NVIDIA Vera Rubin and AMD Instinct MI455X systems in production environments. Traditional air cooling cannot handle GPU TDPs above ~700W, making liquid cooling with coldplates the only viable path for high-density AI clusters. CoolIT's 15 kW coldplate per GPU represents a significant advancement in direct liquid cooling capacity. The company positions this as a 'future-proof' solution covering current Blackwell-generation GPUs (700W) through next-generation AI accelerators expected to reach 1,000W+ TDP.

articles.title: Iren targets Australia for 800MW data center campus
articles.body: Iren, the AI infrastructure company that recently completed a strategic partnership with NVIDIA for up to 5 gigawatts of AI infrastructure deployment in the US, is now targeting Australia for an 800 megawatt data center campus. The Australia expansion signals Iren's ambition to build AI infrastructure capacity across multiple geographies beyond its existing US-focused partnerships. The 800MW target is a large-scale commitment that would make Iren one of the largest data center operators in Australia. Australia has been attracting significant data center investment due to its stable political environment, growing tech sector, and demand for sovereign AI infrastructure.

articles.title: AMD EXPO Ultra Low Latency DDR5 memory at same price as current kits
articles.body: AMD announced EXPO Ultra Low Latency DDR5 memory at Computex 2026, claiming the feature will be 'effectively the same price as current kits' while delivering meaningfully improved latency for AI and gaming workloads. The new EXPO Ultra standard will work on existing chipsets but requires new DIMMs. The announcement comes amid the worst DDR5 price crisis in 15 years, with 32GB kits now costing $375 minimum. AMD's claim of price parity is notable in this environment, suggesting OEM/DRAM manufacturer agreements to hold pricing on the new specification despite overall market inflation. The Ultra Low Latency designation targets AI inference workloads where memory access latency directly impacts token generation speed on on-device AI platforms.

articles.title: OpenAI updates Codex for office workers; Anthropic expands Misos to 150 organizations globally
articles.body:
OpenAI has released an updated version of Codex, its AI coding agent, with new features targeting office workers beyond software developers. The update introduces natural language task execution for non-technical workflows, positioning Codex as a general-purpose enterprise AI agent. This follows OpenAI's strategy of expanding Codex from developer-only tooling to broader enterprise automation.

Separately, Anthropic expanded its Misos (previously known as Mythos Preview or Misos) safety testing and red-teaming program to 150 organizations worldwide. Misos features frontier-level capabilities for cybersecurity analysis and is being used by governments and critical infrastructure operators to proactively identify vulnerabilities in their systems before adversaries can exploit them. The dual-use nature of Misos — powerful enough to discover 10,000+ zero-day vulnerabilities in a month — is why the Trump administration's new AI executive order specifically references Anthropic's capabilities as a model justifying the 30-day pre-review framework.

articles.title: 알리바바, 하이브리드 에이전트 '큐원3.7-플러스' 공개
articles.body:
알리바바가 하이브리드 AI 에이전트 '큐원3.7-플러스(Qwen3.7-Plus)'를 공개했다. 이 모델은 알리바바 클라우드의 큐원 AI 시리즈 최신작으로, 복잡한 다단계 추론 태스크와 실시간 웹 탐색, 코드 실행, 도구 사용을 결합한 하이브리드 에이전트 아키텍처를 채택했다.

큐원3.7-플러스는 기존 모델 대비 특히 수학, 과학, 코딩 등 추론 집약적 태스크에서 성능이 향상됐다. 알리바바는 '이익보다 AI 점유율 우선' 전략을 공개 선언한 바 있으며, 공격적인 가격 정책과 오픈소스 모델 공개를 통해 글로벌 AI 시장에서 영향력을 확대하고 있다. 딥시크의 API 가격 75% 영구 인하(GPT-5.5의 34분의 1)와 함께 중국 AI 기업들의 가격 경쟁이 치열해지고 있다.

articles.title: 스페이스X, IPO서 '1.75조달러' 몸값 도전
articles.body:
스페이스X(SpaceX)가 기업공개(IPO)에서 1.75조 달러(약 2경4000조 원)의 기업 가치를 목표로 하고 있다고 보도됐다. 스페이스X는 인공위성 인터넷 서비스 스타링크(Starlink)와 로켓 제조·발사 사업의 급성장으로 세계 최대 비상장 기업 반열에 올라 있다.

이 IPO는 AI 인프라와 직결되는 측면이 있다: 스타링크는 전 세계 데이터센터와 원격 AI 컴퓨팅 엣지 간 연결에 활용되고 있으며, 스페이스X의 테라팹(Terafab) 반도체 공장 구상(최대 1190억 달러 투자 보도)과도 맞물린다. AI 인프라 투자 물결 속에 스페이스X의 역할이 확대되고 있다.
